newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul security chief warns of drugs from N.Korea.
newsitem.headline: Seoul security chief warns of drugs from N.Korea.

text.p: South Korea's top intelligence official on Wednesday accused North Korea of using drugs and counterfeit money to destabilise the country.

Kwon Young-hae, director of the Agency for National Security Planning, also said Pyongyang was strengthening its links to international terrorist organisations while its economy and society unravelled.
"The North is using counterfeit bills and drugs to disturb social stability in South Korea," Kwon said in a report to the National Assembly.
He said the death of Great Leader Kim Il-sung in 1994 and grinding poverty in the country had led to a breakdown in social values and rising crime.
"One or two years from now we will likely face a grave moment for national security because of the changes that North Korea is undergoing," Kwon said.
He said Pyongyang maintained a 1,700-strong spy force and a 120,000-strong "special military unit".

Kwon did not elaborate on the special unit, but South Korea believes North Korean maintains an elite force of saboteurs and assasins who would be dropped into South Korea by submarine and on aircraft ahead of any invasion.
"North Korea is strengthening training for these units in cooperation with 56 terrorist groups in 35 countries," he said, without identifying the groups or the countries.
Kwon said last month's intrusion by a North Korean submarine had heightened tensions.
"Our security situation has grown strained and military tension has heightened since North Korea's submarine intrusion into the South," he said.
The submarine landed 26 North Koreans on an east coast beach. Twenty-two have been killed and Pyongyang has threathened "merciless retaliation."
